OPERATIVE REPORT

Preoperative Diagnosis: Severe calcific aortic stenosis, native trileaflet valve.
Postoperative Diagnosis: Same.
Procedure Performed: Aortic valve replacement with bioprosthesis via median sternotomy.

Indications: The patient is an elderly individual with progressive dyspnea on exertion and
an echocardiogram demonstrating severe native aortic stenosis with a calculated valve area
of 0.7 cm2. Heart team discussion favored a surgical approach.

Description of Procedure: After induction of general anesthesia, a median sternotomy was
performed and cardiopulmonary bypass was established in standard fashion. The native aortic
valve was heavily calcified and was excised. The annulus was sized and a CE #23 valve was
selected.

Tissue Implant Type: Bioprosthesis
Valve Type Used: Carpentier-Edwards Perimount
Implant Size: 23

The valve was seated without paravalvular leak on intraoperative transesophageal
echocardiography. The patient was weaned from bypass without difficulty.

Intraoperative Echocardiography: Post-implant assessment showed a well-seated prosthetic
valve with a mean gradient of 11 mmHg and no more than trivial paravalvular regurgitation.

Disposition: The patient was transferred to the cardiac surgical intensive care unit in
stable condition.
